content: Nicotine skin patches are prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking by providing a controlled source of nicotine, which helps alleviate withdrawal symptoms associated with smoking cessation. Nicotine patches are designed for direct application to the skin. They should be applied once daily, ideally at the same time each day. These patches are available in different strengths and are used for varying durations, depending on the specific treatment plan. It is essential to follow the instructions on the prescription label precisely. If there is any confusion, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the patches exactly as directed, without altering the dosage or frequency unless instructed by your healthcare provider. To apply the patch, select a clean, dry, and hairless area of skin, such as the upper chest, upper arm, or hip, as specified in the package instructions. Avoid applying the patch to areas of skin that are irritated, oily, scarred, or broken. Remove the patch from its packaging, peel off the protective strip, and immediately place the adhesive side onto your skin. Press the patch firmly in place with the palm of your hand for approximately 10 seconds, ensuring it adheres securely, particularly around the edges. After application, wash your hands with water only (avoid soap) to remove any residual nicotine. If the patch becomes loose or falls off, replace it with a new one. The patch should be worn continuously for 16 to 24 hours, depending on the specific instructions provided with the product. It can be worn while showering or bathing. When removing the patch, fold it in half with the adhesive sides together and dispose of it properly. Apply the next patch to a different area of skin to minimize the risk of irritation. Never wear more than one patch at a time. After the initial two weeks of treatment, your doctor may recommend transitioning to a lower-strength patch. Gradual reduction in patch strength is advised to help manage nicotine withdrawal symptoms. The duration of use typically ranges from 6 to 20 weeks, depending on the specific instructions provided with the patches. Before using nicotine patches, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to adhesive tape or medications. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately, as nicotine and nicotine patches may harm the fetus. If you become pregnant while using the patches, contact your doctor right away. Do not smoke or use other nicotine products while using the patches, as this can lead to nicotine overdose. If you forget to apply a patch, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply two patches to compensate for a missed dose. Nicotine patches may cause side effects. Common, less severe side effects include dizziness, headache, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, and redness or swelling at the application site. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as severe rash or swelling, seizures, abnormal heart rhythm, or difficulty breathing, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a severe reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store nicotine patches in their original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep them at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store them in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused patches by folding them with the adhesive sides together and keeping them out of reach of children and pets. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while using nicotine patches. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Brand names for nicotine patches include Nicoderm® CQ® Clear Step 3, NicoDerm® CQ® Step 1, NicoDerm® CQ® Step 2, NicoDerm® CQ® Step 3, Nicotrol® NS, Nicotrol® Step 1, Nicotrol® Step 2, and Nicotrol® Step 3.
